summary: P. De Lacy Johnstone (1848–1927) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, at the University of Oxford from around 1867 to 1870 as a Boden Sanskrit Scholar, and at Balliol College, Oxford (1868–1876).
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, where he was attested from 1976 to 1988 and again in 2002.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay works in philosophy and Indology. He is a former Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was attested as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 2009.

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1908–1992) studied Indology and philosophy under traditional teacher A. Chinnaswami Sastri (~1928–1935). He was an assistant at Banaras Hindu University (~1935–1942) and Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1968).

Pramod P. Joglekar works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an editor and Regulating Council member at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and is attested as Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College in 2026.

Indologist P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri studied at the University of Madras and Oxford. He served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Professor at Presidency College, Chennai, and Head of Sanskrit at Presidency University.
P. Perumal works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as a part-time conservator at Saraswathi Mahal Library in 1980 and earned an M.L.I.Sc. from Madurai Kamaraj University in 1985.
P. Pratap Kumar (b. 1952) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indology scholar attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) studied at Bishop Heber College, IASE Saidapet, and the University of Madras. He held posts at Bishop Heber College, the University of Madras, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University.
P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who earned an M.Litt. from the University of Madras by 1956 under V. Raghavan. He was attested as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at the National Sanskrit University in 1965.
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) was an Indology scholar who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under Mysore Hiriyanna from circa 1923 to 1927.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist attested as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute in 1944 and as its head in 1954.

Padma Subrahmanyam (b. 1943) works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University, where she completed research supervised by T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under John Brough. He held a professorship at the University of California, Berkeley, where he later became Professor Emeritus.
Pagorn Singsuriya works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Chulalongkorn University and was attested in the humanities faculty at Mahidol University in 2021.

Palden Gyal is a scholar of Tibetology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Duke, Harvard, and Columbia. In 2026, he was a Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University's Heyman Center for the Humanities.

Pallabi Bagchi specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Jadavpur University and earned her Ph.D. at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, where she also worked as a teaching assistant from 2022 to 2025.
Palmer Boyd (1840–1875) was an Indologist who held a post at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1862–1865). He also completed his B.A. there (1867–1871), studying under Edward Byles Cowell in 1867.

Palmira Brummett (b. 1950) studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. A scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, she taught at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and Brown University.
